note: Ten bipolar axes. Structure after the public-domain IPIP item pool (ipip.ori.org); every word here is original to Pathfinder GM (2026-09-25). A score is rolled on a bell curve (3d6 scaled to 0-100): 40-60 is the silent middle and says nothing. Below 40 speaks the low pole, above 60 the high pole; the three words are for 25-39 / 61-75, 10-24 / 76-90, and the extremes. A person is voiced by their two most extreme axes (three when a third is past 85 or under 15). Each pole's id is the tag other tables are checked against. shows: one line of how it comes out in a scene, for the model. No cross-axis exclusions: opposites share one axis, so they cannot both be rolled, and every pairing across axes reads as a person (a timid gossip, a kind miser) — contradiction is what the other tables are checked against these tags for.

low.shows: watches hands before faces and asks why before how

high.shows: takes people at their word and is hurt when that fails

low.shows: lets insults slide past as if they were weather

high.shows: flares fast, cools fast, and says the worst of it in between

low.shows: answers questions with questions and gives away little

high.shows: says the true thing first and the kind thing never

low.shows: pays for others without being asked and forgets it at once

high.shows: knows the price of everything and haggles over the last copper

low.shows: treats omens as jokes and temples as buildings

high.shows: marks the day's small rites and sees the gods' hand in chance

low.shows: keeps a door at their back and a reason to leave ready

high.shows: steps forward before anyone else has decided to

low.shows: speaks when there is something to say and not otherwise

high.shows: knows everybody's news and shares it freely

low.shows: loses things, finds others, and does not mind either way

high.shows: keeps everything in its place and notices when it is not

low.shows: turns praise aside and credits somebody else

high.shows: wants their work and name noticed, and says so if they are not

low.shows: judges by results and does not soften a refusal

high.shows: cannot pass somebody in trouble without stopping

rank.note: How somebody feels about the rich and powerful. Owner ruling 2026-10-01: a lie about who you are that is believed moves the listener by how they feel about what you claimed, and somebody who hates the rich and powerful takes a claim of rank badly. Kept OUT of `axes` on purpose: those ten are rolled in order from one seeded stream, and an eleventh in the loop would re-roll every later trait, want and quirk for everybody met from now on. This one is rolled from its own seed (`lives.rank_score`), so it is the same for a person met yesterday as for one met tomorrow. Same bell curve and the same 40/60 poles as the ten; `bias` shifts it by the work class (`occupations.json` class), the way a priest cannot mock the gods: a noble's steward leans one way and a cutpurse the other. Not voiced as a trait word yet; it is read by `rules/bluff.py` and said through the tell.

low.shows: straightens up and minds their words when somebody of standing is near

high.shows: has a hard word for anyone who never worked for what they have
